newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska corn maturity jumps to 91 percent.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska corn maturity jumps to 91 percent.

text.p: Nebraska's corn development progressed rapidly last week and as of Sunday, 91 percent was mature, up from 67 percent a week ago, equal to 91 percent a year ago and ahead of the 89 percent average, according to the Nebraska Agricultural Statistics Service.
Seven percent of the crop was harvested as of Sunday, up from three percent last week, equal to last year's pace and behind the 20 percent average pace.
Twenty-two percent of the soybean crop was harvested, up from two percent a week ago and ahead of 18 percent a year ago but behind the 45 percent average.
Two percent of the sorghum crop was harvested, behind nine percent a year ago as well as the 22 percent average.
Eighty-eight percent of the wheat crop had been sown, up from 56 percent a week ago but behind 90 percent a year ago and also behind the 94 percent average pace.
Topsoil moisture was rated four percent short, 93 percent adequate and three percent surplus. Subsoil moisture levels were five percent short, 92 percent adequate and three percent surplus.
